description: Me apasiona convertir problemas reales en soluciones digitales. Aporto desarrollo de software, integración de datos, mapas y uso de IA, con enfoque en prototipos útiles y trabajo organizado. En Field Shift quiero conectar datos de la NASA con decisiones agrícolas claras. Busco personas con interés en agronomía, análisis de datos, teledetección, programación o diseño.
summary: Field Shift is a bilingual (English/Spanish) web app that dives from orbit to one farmer's field and turns NASA Earth data into a cited pre-diagnosis for crop rotation and pest care. The farmer picks or draws a field, tells an AI consultant what grows now, what grew before and how the field is watered, and sends photos. Field Shift reads NASA POWER (40 years of weather and degree-days for pest generations), SMAP soil moisture, GPM IMERG rain, GRACE/GRACE-FO water storage, the GEOS-FP forecast, NASADEM slope and NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 projections, together with Sentinel-2 and Landsat crop vigor at 10-30 m. It then compares the farmer's current rotation with two alternatives, ranks the pests likely on that field, names the natural enemies and beneficial fungi to protect, and exports a technical sheet where every number shows its source, date and scale (field-level or regional). It was shaped with an agronomist in the Huaral valley, Peru, where warmer seasons make pests breed faster and sprays more frequent. It supports, and never replaces, the farmer's agronomist.
details:
From orbit to one farmer's field

Field Shift turns free NASA Earth data into a cited, field-level plan for crop rotation and pest care, in the farmer's own language (English or Spanish). It answers the challenge end to end: it compares the farmer's current rotation with two alternatives and, for each one, shows why it was suggested, the evidence, the benefits, the information gaps and the risks to check locally. Every result is a pre-diagnosis that the farmer's agronomist confirms.

The problem

  • Up to 40% of the world's crop production is lost to pests every year (FAO, 2021).
  • Warming speeds pests up. In our pilot field in the Huaral valley, Peru, this season runs about 5 °C warmer than its 40-year normal and pea aphids complete about three more generations than normal.
  • Farmers answer with more frequent sprays, which raise costs and harm soil life (agronomist interview, Huaral).

How it works, in four steps

  1. Your field. GPS, place search, an example site, a point or a drawn outline; the area is measured for you.
  2. Tell it what you know. A short form or a guided chat: crop now, crops before, watering, soil and priorities. "I don't know" is a valid answer and becomes a declared gap. Full-resolution photos and voice dictation in English and Spanish.
  3. NASA reads your field. An evidence package for the exact coordinates, where every reading carries its source, date, resolution and a field-level or regional context badge.
  4. A plan to act. Dashboard, Prevention, Organic care, Rotation with "What if I grow…?", and a downloadable technical sheet, CSV data and a share link.

NASA data at the core

  • NASA POWER: 40 years of weather; heat, rain, FAO-56 evapotranspiration, water balance and degree-days for pest generations.
  • SMAP L4: soil moisture against the same date in past years.
  • GPM IMERG: satellite rain over the last 30 days.
  • GRACE/GRACE-FO: long-term water storage.
  • GEOS-FP: the 9-day forecast that drives the pest-prevention lights.
  • NASADEM: the slope of the field. NEX-GDDP-CMIP6: 2031–2050 climate to stress-test each rotation.
  • Landsat and ESA Sentinel-2: crop vigor and bare-soil periods at 10–30 m, on the field itself.

What makes it different

  • The field is the unit. The app dives from orbit to one outline and shows, at true size, which data describe that field and which only describe the region.
  • Pest pressure is computed, not guessed: published degree-day thresholds on NASA temperatures, plus the forecast.
  • Integrated pest management first: natural enemies such as lady beetles and parasitoid wasps, beneficial fungi such as Trichoderma, and when to act, instead of more chemicals.
  • An honest AI consultant: it may only cite numbers from the evidence package, asks for what is missing (for example, a closer photo of the underside of a leaf) and marks every gap.
  • Rotations ready for the future: options tested against 2031–2050 projections; any crop can be evaluated on the farmer's own field.

Built to be trusted

  • A value without a source is an information gap, never a guess; recent NASA POWER days are labelled provisional.
  • Crop traits, pest thresholds and natural enemies come from a cited knowledge base (FAO-56, FAO Ecocrop, UC IPM, SARE, INIA, SENASA, peer-reviewed papers); AI-researched items are labelled "AI-researched, verify".
  • The advice was shaped with agronomist Ing. Cenia, who works with farmers in Huaral.
  • Open source (Apache-2.0), with every source and licence listed.

Impact

Small farmers get a free, bilingual decision tool that brings NASA's global data down to their own field and moves them from more spraying toward integrated pest management and soil care. NASA POWER, SMAP, GPM, GRACE and the satellites used are global, so the same four steps work for fields anywhere. Huaral is the first.

Tech stack

Rust (axum, tokio, sqlx, reqwest) and MariaDB · TypeScript and Vite · Three.js globe · Leaflet and MapLibre · Claude (Anthropic API) for the consultant · Gemini for voice dictation · Google Cloud e2-micro with Caddy (HTTPS) · domain from the Space Apps global offer · films made in code with Lemo-Opuscar.

Try it

  • Open the finished example (loads in seconds)

  • How-to film, 2:21 (English) · Cómo funciona, 2:21 (Spanish)
